pr_title: fix(common): date is not correctly formatted when year is between 0 and 99
pr_body:
…nd 99

use setFullYear method when parsing date to avoid javascript date factory behaviour, which converts year between 0 and 99 to 1900 - 1999

Fixes #40377

@abarghoud - the projects that use Angular internally all use the same version: the current master branch! @AndrewKushnir @petebacondarwin, Actually I wrote a test that reproduces the failing test but I got a different failing result than what you posted, the result I got is: 
` Expected 'Sep 19, 2019, 5:00:00 PM UTC-07:00' to equal 'Sep 20, 2019, 12:00:00 AM UTC-07:00'.`
and I think that it's the correct behaviour as we set the timezone to `-7` so `Sep 20, 2019, 12:00:00 AM UTC` `-7` equals `Sep 19, 2019, 5:00:00 PM UTC-07:00`

I also checked the stackblitz that you sent, it gives `Date: Sep 20, 2019, 12:00:00 AM UTC+02:00` but when defining timezone to `-7` it become `Date: Sep 19, 2019, 3:00:00 PM UTC-07:00` which is correct too giving browser timezone is `UTC+02:00`
https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-repro-40448-nlvq6o?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.html

and of course, I get a different result again, since I am in a different timezone to either of you:

```
Date: Sep 19, 2019, 4:00:00 PM UTC-07:00
```

So I think the point is that, previously, our date-time parsing was locale specific, whereas this PR makes the parsing locale agnostic. From looking at our docs, we claim that passing a string to `DatePipe`/`formatDate()` is evaluated as an [ISO Date-time string](https://angular.io/api/common/formatDate), which is defined in the [ECMAScript specification](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-time-string-format). But the spec doesn't say what the default times should be for date only strings.

Looking into this further I found the [MDN doc](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Date/parse#date_time_string_format) which states:

>  When the time zone offset is absent, date-only forms are interpreted as a UTC time and date-time forms are interpreted as local time.

So if we were to follow that, then `2019-09-20` should be interpreted as UTC (as in this PR) but if any time is included - e.g. `2019-09-20T00:00:00` then it should default to the local time (assuming no timezone value was provided).

---

I think this means that this PR is actually a breaking change - but a valid one, that we should look to roll out for v12. I don't know how much impact this would have in G3...

> I don't know how much impact this would have in G3...

```

is saying that the date should be treated with timezone of `+0`, which is UTC, rather than the local system timezone.

This seems to me exactly what we are doing in this PR. In other words, I don't understand why that particular application would fail in this case since the caller is specifically asking for a UTC date... Or am I missing something?

Here is an example: https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-wbcnan?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.html

> @petebacondarwin, the issues are mostly in tests, but there is a couple failures in app logic, one of them passes params to a function but applies date pipe transformation before doing that, i.e. something like this:
>

> ```
> 
> Also most of other failures have similar origin: while processing date (without time part), there are expectations that the time would be set as midnight (similar to what I mentioned before). I believe this is something that other people might expect as well...
> 
> After looking at the test cases and apps code, I feel like the breaking change might be relatively substantial with arguably less expected new behavior. Would it be possible to keep existing behavior and just fix the original issue (for 0-99 range)?

Hello @AndrewKushnir, In order to make this fix and keep existing behavior, I would like you to confirm to me the current behaviors that we've identified until this moment, so I can write some unit tests that covers them in the code:

1. There is one here https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/40448#issuecomment-761880672 which we've considered as a valid breaking change, would it still be considered as a valid behavior ?
2. The other one is https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/40448#issuecomment-765076140 which I cannot reproduce, I've added some unit tests to test that giving a date without time part the time should be set to midnight, and these tests are passing.

@petebacondarwin @AndrewKushnir what do you think ?

I guess we need to decide whether a date-only string should be parsed as UTC-0 or parsed as though it is midnight in the local timezone.

The `Date()` constructor, which I believe works the same way as `Date.parse()` as string that contains no time parts should be treated as UTC.See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Date/Date#Timestamp_string

> Support for ISO 8601 formats differs in that date-only strings (e.g. "1970-01-01") are treated as UTC, not local.

So I think that this breaking change really is what we want. I think the workaround for apps that expect it to be local is to add a time to the string. For example:

```ts
formatDate('2019-09-20T00:00:00')
```

issue_context.title: angular v11 - bug in 2 functions in angular/packages/common/src/i18n/format_date.ts
comments:
Summarizing here: this is a bug with date **parsing** (not formatting). The `Date` constructor treats the `year` parameter specially, such that if it's a value between `0` and `99`, it "helpfully" makes it `1900` - `1999`. The behavior here should use `setFullYear` to make the behavior consistent.

Updated stackblitz that shows the issue from Pete: 
https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-5hb4hr?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.html
